title: Folded Door and Wall Handset Call Booth
description: One newly authored complete fixed public call-booth exterior and open interior. A continuous four-corner framed shell has real open side windows and one solid rear mounting wall above an integral ground floor. A low flat roof closes the top. Two entire thick windowed entrance leaves form one fixed inward-folded pair around a continuous common hinge and left jamb, leaving the remaining front opening empty. A newly drawn wall-mounted phone body has real blind coin and return recesses, a blank keypad and one whole vertically bridged bulb-ended handset on a short bracket; one continuous curved cord returns to that same body. This is not the old table telephone placed into a service-window kiosk: no desktop base, rotary finger wheel, front counter, hipped striped roof or rear staff door is imported. Every visible surface is newly authored. Four opaque untextured PBR roles, metre Z-up ground-centred envelope; one model zero scenes. Side and door windows are deliberately unglazed real openings, no transparent glass promise. Static artistic depiction only: no calling, signal, circuit, payment, sound, door travel, privacy, weatherproofing, human fit, accessible passage, occupancy, manufacture, installation or safety capability. Rigging animation and interaction not made.
